# Decision history — bpg-rs

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## bpg.decision.canonical-slow-variant-c

### Revision 1 — Canonical Slow search switched from cheap-top-1 to promoted-exact variant-C

`active` · `@bpg.decision.canonical-slow-variant-c/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/stillsearch/**"` · topic `slow-search-shape`

Canonical `Slow` search mode is switched from the legacy
cheap-winner/materialize-winner shortcut to the promoted-exact
variant-C shape. The legacy shortcut is retained only behind
`BPG_STILLSEARCH_SLOW_AUDIT_VARIANT=A`/`legacy` for comparison.

**Context.** Sparse-oracle sampling found the legacy cheap-top-1 decision matched the full-mode winner only 51.5-58.3% of the time across single-image and 10-source samples, while the rough shortlist itself contained the winner 88-95% of the time - the risk was early finalization, not shortlist coverage.

**Consequences.** Variant-C moves the hot profile into exact mode evaluation (LumaExact 43.5%, ForwardXform 46.1% of substage time), which is why later SIMD work targeted the exact-evaluation path rather than the cheap shortlist.

## bpg.decision.canvas-journal-undo-model

### Revision 1 — Canvas rollback uses an undo journal, not x265's per-depth buffer copy-up

`active` · `@bpg.decision.canvas-journal-undo-model/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/**"` · topic `canvas-rollback-model`

Phase 1 of the canvas implements rollback via an undo journal
rather than adopting x265's per-RQT-depth reconstruction buffer
copy-up shape.

**Context.** x265's shape cannot implement `OverlayCache` (it has no `mark`/`detach` analogue), so it forfeits the drop-in A/B and byte-identity-by-construction that the journal gives phase 1.

**Consequences.** The journal keeps search code untouched for phase 1. If the canvas wins and the trait is later simplified in phase 2, converting the journal to per-depth rectangles becomes a contained follow-up inside the canvas type - which is what phase 2 (patch overlay and border cache retirement) then did.

## bpg.decision.canvas-u16-storage

### Revision 1 — Canvas backing buffer is u16 for every bit depth, including 8-bit

`active` · `@bpg.decision.canvas-u16-storage/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/**"` · topic `canvas-storage-width`

The contiguous per-CTU canvas stores samples as `u16` for every bit
depth, not `u8` even when encoding 8-bit content.

**Context.** An alternative u8-canvas-plus-validity-bitmap design was considered and rejected as "complexity not worth it before phase-1 numbers exist". The canvas background uses `UNINIT_SAMPLE = u16::MAX` as an availability sentinel, which does not fit in u8; clamping it to 255 destroys the sentinel because 255 is a legal pixel value, silently corrupting decisions - the exact failure mode already hit once with zero-filled worker frames.

**Consequences.** 33 KB/component per CTU stays L2-resident, and readers that already produce u16/i32 border arrays need no conversion. The sentinel is preserved by construction.

## bpg.decision.chroma-dm-reuse-conservative

### Revision 1 — Chroma DM state is reused only for the commit path, on the already-pruned rough path

`active` · `@bpg.decision.chroma-dm-reuse-conservative/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/**"` · topic `chroma-search-cost-reuse`

The shipped chroma search keeps exact DM (derived-mode)
recomputation for the cost comparison, and only reuses DM state for
the commit path, and only on the already-pruned (intentionally
non-identical) rough path.

**Context.** The original plan proposed reusing the stored DM plan-block cost as the DM baseline directly, which changed decisions and was rejected. The shipped, more conservative design keeps output byte-identical to the old exhaustive path with `CHROMA_ROUGH=0` or `CHROMA_ROUGH_K=4` plus skip off (verified sha256-equal).

**Consequences.** Retains about 98% of the chroma RGB BD-rate gain while cutting about 75% of the exact chroma work and about 27% of the added time on the 14-image calibration set.

## bpg.decision.finalize-skip-not-shipped

### Revision 1 — Finalize re-code skip is not shipped; the finalize pass stays load-bearing

`active` · `@bpg.decision.finalize-skip-not-shipped/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/rdoq.rs"` · topic `finalize-recode-skip`

The proposed skip of the decoder-order `RdoqFinal` finalize walk,
substituting retained search-time coefficients and reconstruction,
is not shipped. The finalize pass remains load-bearing for
recon/decode equality.

**Context.** An attempt found the divergence between retained search state and the decoder-order finalize walk too broad: retained coefficients and reconstruction are not a drop-in substitute.

**Consequences.** This closes off one of the six audit-listed speed levers; a correctness-equality investigation (finalize equality) would need to land first before any future finalize-skip attempt.

## bpg.decision.hybrid-cpu-worker-cap

### Revision 1 — WPP worker count is capped at performance-core thread count on narrow wavefronts

`active` · `@bpg.decision.hybrid-cpu-worker-cap/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/write.rs"` · topic `hybrid-cpu-scheduling`

On hybrid-topology CPUs, the default WPP worker count is capped at
the performance-core thread count when rows are narrow enough that
efficiency cores would otherwise be assigned a wavefront slot.

**Context.** The 12 MP residual gap versus C was root-caused to parallel scheduling efficiency on a hybrid i7-13700H, not per-thread kernel throughput, which was already at parity or better.

**Consequences.** Fresh 7-image sweep moved from 1.056x to 1.040x aggregate after this cap landed, on the way to the final 1.016x after root-TU dedup.

## bpg.decision.psy-off-by-default

### Revision 1 — psy-rd and psy-rdoq are off-by-default, opt-in levers

`active` · `@bpg.decision.psy-off-by-default/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/stillsearch/**"` · topic `psy-levers-default-state`

x265's two psychovisual energy-preservation levers, `psy_rd` and
`psy_rdoq`, are ported to still265 off by default and opt-in via
config and CLI, tunable for the AQ/perceptual-quality effort.

**Context.** The goal was parity with x265's psychovisual tooling without changing default output for callers who never opt in.

**Consequences.** Every new code path is guarded behind `psy_rd > 0` / `psy_rdoq > 0`, and the ported weight kernel was verified to match x265's `rdcost.h` shape.

## bpg.decision.rdoq-int64-cost-domain

### Revision 1 — Port RDOQ's cost domain to x265's exact int64 fixed point

`active` · `@bpg.decision.rdoq-int64-cost-domain/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/rdoq.rs"` · topic `rdoq-arithmetic-domain`

RDOQ's cost domain is ported from scalar f64 arithmetic to x265's
exact int64 fixed-point arithmetic, as one atomic unit rather than
a partial port.

**Context.** `rdoq_single_scan_into` was deeply f64-based against x265's fixed-point int64 plus assembly. A partial port would change decisions and fail BD/recon parity, so it had to be ported as one atomic unit with `lambda2`/`scaleBits` seeded exactly from x265.

**Consequences.** BD-rate +0.002% (12 MP) / +0.0001% (50 MP) over QP 22-34 - neutral; wall -1% single-thread. The f64 arithmetic turned out not to be the RDOQ bottleneck, which re-scoped the follow-on vectorization work (see @bpg.decision.rdoq-vectorization-rescoped).

## bpg.decision.rdoq-vectorization-rescoped

### Revision 1 — AVX2 residual-pricing vectorization is re-scoped, not implemented as originally planned

`active` · `@bpg.decision.rdoq-vectorization-rescoped/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/rdoq.rs"` · topic `rdoq-vectorization`

The originally-planned `costCoeffNxN`-style AVX2 vectorization of
residual pricing is not implemented as scoped; the approach is
re-scoped pending further design.

**Context.** still265's pricing sink evolves CABAC-style contexts per bin, so sig-flag/C1/C2 costing is a serial dependency chain through the context models - x265's SIMD shape does not map onto it directly.

**Consequences.** Vectorization work on residual pricing is deferred behind a redesign of the pricing sink rather than attempted as a direct port.

## bpg.decision.ssim-aq-active-under-cqp

### Revision 1 — CQP mode must still be able to emit spatial AQ via legal cu_qp_delta

`proposed` · `@bpg.decision.ssim-aq-active-under-cqp/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/**"` · topic `ssim-tune-aq-interaction`

still265 should not mimic x265's behavior of disabling adaptive
quantization under CQP rate control. Instead it needs a
still-image-specific rule: CQP may still use spatial AQ by emitting
legal per-QG `cu_qp_delta` syntax.

**Context.** x265 forcibly clears AQ under CQP and warns that SSIM-tune with AQ off is invalid, which would make an SSIM-RD-style mode pointless for a CQP-only still encoder. A minimal, experimental `ssim_rd`/`ssim_rd_weight` scalar has landed (env-gated, `SSIM_RD`/`SSIM_RD_WEIGHT`), but the fuller CTU-normalized `SsimNorm`/`Tune::Ssim` design this decision describes, and the guaranteed-active-AQ-under-CQP behavior with its three named regression tests, had not been confirmed shipped as of this ledger's authoring.

**Consequences.** Any future SSIM-tune work must prove AQ is exercised by checking that `cu_qp_delta` is actually emitted, not just that the analysis cost changed.

## bpg.decision.wpp-geometry-aware-release-policy

### Revision 1 — Unset WPP release policy becomes geometry-aware (stall-only under 96 CTUs wide)

`active` · `@bpg.decision.wpp-geometry-aware-release-policy/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/write.rs"` · topic `wpp-release-cadence`

The unset/`auto` WPP release policy is geometry-aware instead of
unconditionally K=4: rows narrower than 96 CTUs default to
stall-only, rows 96 CTUs or wider default to K=4.

**Context.** Interleaved sweeps found stall-only had the best 12 MP min/mean, while K=4 had the best 50 MP mean - no single fixed K served both geometries well.

**Consequences.** Replaces the flat K=4 default from @bpg.decision.wpp-release-coarsening with a per-row-width rule; the env override remains available for manual tuning.

**supersedes** `@bpg.decision.wpp-release-coarsening/1`

## bpg.decision.wpp-notify-one-wakeup

### Revision 1 — Normal WPP handoff progress wakes one claimer, not the whole pool

`active` · `@bpg.decision.wpp-notify-one-wakeup/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/write.rs"` · topic `wpp-wakeup-policy`

Normal handoff progress wakes one sleeping claimer per CTU instead
of broadcasting to the whole pool after every CTU. The whole-row
fallback path (`BPG_WPP_HANDOFF=0`, worker-frame fallback, AQ-WPP
tree builds) intentionally keeps notify-all.

**Context.** Targets ping-pong/claim-mutex overhead from broadcasting on every CTU. The fallback exception exists because workers blocked on a dependency inside an already-claimed row are not counted by `idle_claimers`, so notify-one there could strand a runnable row.

**Consequences.** Reduces wakeup churn on the common path while preserving correctness on the excluded, scheduling-shaped paths.

## bpg.decision.wpp-release-coarsening

### Revision 1 — Voluntary WPP frontier release coarsened to every 4 completed CTUs

`superseded` · `@bpg.decision.wpp-release-coarsening/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/write.rs"` · topic `wpp-release-cadence`

Voluntary idle-worker releases of the WPP handoff frontier happen
every 4 completed CTUs by default, instead of every CTU. Dependency
stalls still park immediately.

**Context.** First Linux numbers showed the large smooth 50 MP case at parity/noise (~0.95x of `bpgenc -m9`) but the 12 MP case still around ~1.25x, motivating a tunable release cadence.

**Consequences.** Made tunable via `BPG_WPP_HANDOFF_RELEASE`; later refined into a geometry-aware policy (see @bpg.decision.wpp-geometry-aware-release-policy).

**superseded by** `@bpg.decision.wpp-geometry-aware-release-policy/1`
